title: Thad Jones and violinist Ray Perry sit in
summary: Thad Jones loses his job by sitting in nightly, and Sam praises Ray Perry's Parker-like jazz violin and the Perry brothers.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Thad Jones used to come down there then. Well, Thad Jones got fired from messing around--down there messing around with us. He wouldn't go to work. He came down there playing with us every night. And, you know, when he decided to go to work, he didn't have no job.
Was he with Basie?

No, he was--he came down there with a show. He was working on Miami Beach. I forgot the name of the band he was working with. And I'll tell you another guy used to come and set in with us by the name of Ray Perry.
Ray Perry--yeah.
He was a jazz violinist player.
Uh huh.

He was a really a truly a jazz violinist, man. I don't know these people talking about people I heard playing jazz violin. You know, they good and stuff, man, you know. But I--they ain't nothing you can jump up and click your heels about. This man--this man sound like Charlie Parker, man, on the violin.
Hmm.
I mean, his phrase--
I heard--I heard him. Ray Perry, yeah.
He died. It was about four brothers-- Babe Perry, Ray Perry, you know. And all the brothers played.
Babe Perry was a drummer. He was a pretty good drummer, too.
Uh huh.
But Ray Perry, man. And he was playing and he was also an alto player saxophone.
Uh huh.
And he worked in the Illinois Jacquet band. Remember that hell of a band Illinois had?
Yeah.
Well, he was the alto player in that band.
Uh huh.

But he played--the only solos he played it on the violin. And he came spent the night with us every night, man. All of the--I got to know a lot of musicians. When I came to New York, I already knew everybody. Well, anyway, we didn't go back down there. We quit.
